subject: Workplace Skills
title: Habit Stacking for Consistency
description: A quick, practical guide to Habit Stacking for Consistency.

hook.text: BJ Fogg's research at Stanford shows new habits stick best when anchored to an existing routine.

buildup.text: Habit stacking is linking a new behavior to a current one: after I pour coffee, I review my three priorities.

discovery.text: The existing habit acts as a cue. No willpower needed because the trigger is already automated in your brain.

twist.text: Stacking only works if the anchor habit is solid. Attaching to an inconsistent trigger builds nothing.

climax.text: Pick your most reliable daily habit. Attach one tiny new behavior. Only add another after 14 days.

punchline.text: Stack new on stable. One habit at a time.

quiz.question: Why does habit stacking work effectively?
options: It replaces old habits with new ones
The existing habit acts as an automatic trigger
It requires intense willpower to maintain
